summary: Regime read: Potential pivot → tightening. Of the weighted evidence, 48% points tightening, 33% mixed, and 19% easing. Inflation is strongly tightening (per Reuters: US inflation surprise offers Warsh only brief relief). Fed communications are strongly tightening (per Federal Reserve: Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell press conference after the July 2026 FOMC meeting). Employment is leaning easing and market pricing is strongly tightening.
what_would_change_the_call: A second consecutive upside inflation surprise.
Front-end (2Y) yields rising materially further over the intermeeting window.
A Fed official explicitly pushing back against near-term cuts.
Fed funds futures repricing from 'fewer cuts' toward outright hikes.

checklist.text: Fed communications explicitly de-emphasize further easing
Fed emphasizes inflation upside risks over labor weakness
Market pricing removes expected cuts or starts pricing hikes
2Y yields rise materially over the intermeeting window
Inflation data surprises to the upside
Employment remains firm enough to reduce pressure for cuts
SPY/TLT color and rate-market behavior confirm the macro read

scoring.method: weighted vote-share over source direction, one vote per event cluster (no magnitude averaging)
scoring.clustering: one vote per event_key; representative = max-weight source; keyless sources are singleton clusters

sources.evidence_text: Initial jobless claims fell by 4,000 to 226,000 for the week ending June 13, while continuing claims rose to 1.81 million for the prior week.

sources.title: U.S. weekly jobless claims fall to 226,000 in June 2026

sources.why_it_matters: The mixed data of a falling weekly average but rising continuing claims reflects a stable but not weakening labor market, offering no strong directional pressure for the Fed.

sources.title: Elevated energy prices increase investor expectations for higher policy rates later this year
sources.evidence_text: Investors now expect higher policy rates later in 2026 due to elevated energy prices, reversing earlier expectations for one to two cuts.
sources.why_it_matters: Inflationary pressure from energy prices pushes the Fed's reaction function toward tightening to protect the 2% target.

sources.why_it_matters: The combination of high headline inflation and core inflation above target provides strong justification for the Fed to maintain a restrictive stance.

sources.title: Federal Reserve issues FOMC statement
sources.evidence_text: The FOMC kept the federal funds target range at 3.50% to 3.75% and said it remains committed to its dual-mandate objectives.
sources.why_it_matters: A hold signals the Fed is not yet ready to ease further, but it also is not tightening, so the labor market data must weaken further to justify cuts.

sources.title: Warsh kicks off Fed chief era with sweeping review as rates remain unchanged
sources.evidence_text: Reuters reported that officials left rates unchanged while new quarterly projections showed nine of 19 policymakers expected a rate hike by the end of 2026.
sources.why_it_matters: A shift in the dot plot toward hikes signals a reaction function that is becoming less supportive of near-term easing.

sources.title: Fed Decision in June? Trading Odds & Predictions 2026
sources.evidence_text: CME FedWatch pricing a hold above 96% and no material shift in expectations over the past week, reflecting persistent inflation pressures and a resilient labor market.
sources.why_it_matters: Market pricing aligns with the Fed's restrictive stance, reinforcing the reaction function's resistance to easing despite prior expectations of cuts.

sources.why_it_matters: The scenario that policy is significantly too loose for current inflation levels strongly supports a tightening reaction function to close the gap.

sources.title: Fed's next move may be a hike, not a cut, says J.P. Morgan
sources.evidence_text: J.P. Morgan Global Research says it expects the Fed to stay on hold through 2026 and to deliver its next move as a 25 basis point hike in the second half of 2027.
sources.why_it_matters: A major bank forecasting no cuts and a later hike signals a reaction-function view in which inflation persistence dominates growth concerns.

sources.title: June Fed meeting: Here's what changed in the new statement
sources.evidence_text: Wednesday's release omitted details about member voting and forward guidance, with Warsh remarking it 'dispenses with some older language' to give 'just the facts'.
sources.why_it_matters: The removal of forward guidance and voting details reduces market signaling, supporting a neutral stance by avoiding explicit commitments to easing or tightening.

sources.evidence_text: TD said the June statement was pared back, removed prior easing bias, and that the updated median rate path implied possible hikes later in 2026.
sources.why_it_matters: If the forward guidance no longer leans easing and the projected path shifts higher, the reaction function is drifting away from cuts.

sources.title: FOMC Recap: Warsh ushers in new era at the Fed
sources.evidence_text: Warsh's current focus is very clearly directed to inflation over labor, and the Fed Funds Rate projections have been adjusted to reflect a hiking bias in 2026.
sources.why_it_matters: The explicit prioritization of inflation triage over employment suggests a policy stance more likely to hike than cut if inflation pressures persist.

sources.title: FOMC Press Conference, June 17, 2026 | Crypto Craft
sources.evidence_text: FED REMOVES easing bias from forward guidance in the post-meeting statement.
sources.why_it_matters: Removing the easing bias from forward guidance indicates a shift toward a more neutral or tightening policy stance, reducing expectations for future rate cuts.

sources.title: Fed holds rates steady, pares down statement to remove cutting bias
sources.evidence_text: CNBC reported that the Fed removed language implying a near-term cutting bias and that officials' projections pointed to a higher year-end funds rate.
sources.why_it_matters: A reduced cutting bias and higher projected policy path both imply less urgency to ease, which can matter more than headline rate holds for the Fed reaction function.

sources.title: June 2026 FOMC Reaction: A Hawkish Hold
sources.evidence_text: The FOMC's primary concern appears to be inflation, not labor market health, with half of the committee members projecting rate hikes this year.
sources.why_it_matters: Prioritizing inflation over labor market health and projecting hikes reinforces a tightening bias in the Fed's policy reaction function.

sources.title: Live updates: Interest rates steady, Federal Reserve forecasts 1 rate cut in 2026
sources.evidence_text: Fed officials now expect inflation, both headline and core, to reach 2.7% by year-end, above the 2% target, while forecasting an unemployment rate of 4.4%.
sources.why_it_matters: Rising inflation forecasts above target with stable unemployment reduce the need for easing, supporting a neutral-to-tightening stance in the Fed's policy calculus.

sources.title: Fed pauses: inflation, oil & smart portfolio moves
sources.evidence_text: Nuveen said the Fed unanimously left rates unchanged at 3.50% to 3.75%.
sources.why_it_matters: A pause is consistent with a data-dependent stance, which keeps the policy path sensitive to whether inflation or labor slack dominates.

sources.title: Trading Fed Rate Probabilities: How to Use the CME FedWatch Tool
sources.evidence_text: Market expectations currently point to potential further rate cuts in the second half of 2026, with June being the earliest likely date.
sources.why_it_matters: This forward-looking market pricing signals that traders anticipate the Fed will ease policy sooner than previously expected, directly influencing the reaction function toward cuts.

sources.evidence_text: 30-Day Fed Funds futures prices imply a 67.9% probability of a rate hike at the next FOMC meeting, with futures pricing in a hike in October and potential for another in December.
sources.why_it_matters: Market-implied probabilities from Fed Funds futures directly inform the Fed’s reaction function by signaling that tightening is expected, reducing the likelihood of cuts.

sources.evidence_text: The CME FedWatch Tool forecasts the probability of a rate hike based on 30-Day Federal Funds futures prices, with current data showing a high likelihood of tightening.
sources.why_it_matters: FedWatch probabilities directly reflect market expectations for tightening, shaping the Fed’s reaction function by signaling reduced cut likelihood.

sources.evidence_text: Fed funds futures are contracts traded on the CME that help predict economic outcomes like rate hikes or cuts.

sources.why_it_matters: The median expectation for one to two rate hikes in 2026 signals a shift from prior cut expectations, directly supporting a tightening bias in the Fed's reaction function.

sources.why_it_matters: Internal FOMC minutes revealing a case for rate hikes due to elevated inflation risks reinforce a tightening orientation in the policy reaction function.

sources.evidence_text: When monetary policy appears less sensitive to financial conditions, financial imbalances tend to grow, potentially exacerbating the financial boom-bust cycles.
sources.why_it_matters: This paper highlights the importance of the Fed’s reaction function to financial stability, but does not provide current policy direction or evidence of easing/tightening.

sources.evidence_text: The study estimates a modified reaction function using money supply as the operational instrument for the Federal Reserve, showing how unconventional measures influence policy decisions.
sources.why_it_matters: While the paper provides a theoretical framework for the Fed's reaction function, it does not directly predict the next FOMC decision, making its impact on easing/tightening expectations neutral.

sources.why_it_matters: Higher PCE inflation reduces the Fed’s room to cut and raises the risk that policy stays restrictive longer.

sources.evidence_text: Core PCE Price Index Annual Change in the United States increased to 3.40 percent in May from 3.30 percent in April of 2026.

sources.why_it_matters: Persistently elevated PCE inflation argues for a more cautious Fed stance and fewer easing signals.

sources.title: Inflation Nowcasting

sources.why_it_matters: Nowcasts can flag whether near-term core inflation momentum is strengthening or easing before the Fed receives official data.

sources.why_it_matters: QT’s dampening effect on inflation reduces the urgency for rate hikes, implying a more easing-friendly stance in the Fed’s reaction function if inflation remains subdued.

sources.title: Why the Fed Could Shrink Its Balance Sheet Again (and Markets Might Not Notice)

sources.evidence_text: The FOMC voted to keep the federal funds rate unchanged at its current range of 3.5% to 3.75%, reinforcing the diminishing urgency in lowering interest rates due to solid economic activity and a stable labor market.

sources.title: Treasury yields rise after Warsh's debut meeting brings hawkish shift

sources.why_it_matters: The dot plot shift toward hikes directly alters the Fed's reaction function by increasing the likelihood of tightening rather than easing.

sources.evidence_text: With inflation expected to remain elevated, rate cuts do not seem likely anytime soon, and the Fed now appears to be in wait-and-see mode.

sources.why_it_matters: Expectations of steady rates amid monitoring inflation and growth suggest a balanced Fed reaction function, keeping 2-year yields neutral.

sources.evidence_text: Jobless claims remain at low levels, signaling sustained labor market strength and resilience.

sources.why_it_matters: The removal of forward guidance increases policy uncertainty and signals a more hawkish, data-dependent approach favoring tighter conditions.

sources.title: FX Daily Snapshot
sources.evidence_text: MUFG says OIS pricing still assigns roughly a 30% chance of a rate hike at the July 29 meeting and that the curve looks too rich for hikes.
sources.why_it_matters: If the market prices a meaningful hike probability, that reduces the expected ease of policy and signals tighter near-term financial conditions.

sources.title: US labor market adds 73,000 jobs in July while May, June reports see larger-than-normal downward revisions
sources.evidence_text: July nonfarm payrolls increased by 73,000, unemployment rose to 4.2%, and average hourly earnings rose 3.9% year over year.
sources.why_it_matters: Slower hiring with still-elevated but not accelerating wages supports the case for easier policy if the Fed is prioritizing labor-market cooling over renewed tightening.

sources.title: US weekly jobless claims plunge to lowest since 1969
sources.evidence_text: Initial jobless claims fell by 22,000 to 187,000 for the week ended July 18, and continuing claims also declined.
sources.why_it_matters: Lower claims signal a still-resilient labor market, which reduces the urgency for Fed cuts and keeps attention on inflation.

sources.title: Weak jobs, declining labor force, could renew Fed debate over state of labor market
sources.evidence_text: Reuters said the weaker jobs report could reopen debate at the Fed about how to read labor-market conditions.
sources.why_it_matters: If officials view weakening hiring as genuine slack rather than supply-side distortion, the reaction function shifts toward fewer tightening risks and more easing room.

sources.title: PCE report: Fed's preferred inflation measure hits 3-year high, keeping talk of possible rate hike in play
sources.evidence_text: The May PCE report showed headline inflation at 4.1% and core PCE at 3.4%, both higher than in April and the strongest readings in roughly three years.
sources.why_it_matters: A hotter PCE print pushes the Fed reaction function toward fewer cuts and preserves the possibility of renewed tightening if inflation persists.

sources.title: Top Fed officials embrace cooler inflation reading, clamor for more
sources.evidence_text: Fed officials said one cooler inflation reading was encouraging but not enough to declare that price pressures are safely receding.
sources.why_it_matters: The Fed is likely to wait for multiple soft prints before easing, so this keeps policy data-dependent rather than clearly dovish.

sources.title: Fed Policymaker Comments Raise the Stakes for Inflation Data
sources.evidence_text: PIMCO said recent Fed comments signaled that another hot core inflation reading could push the FOMC to consider tightening soon.
sources.why_it_matters: Market participants are treating inflation persistence as a trigger for fewer cuts or even renewed tightening.

sources.title: Methodology changes could lower US May core PCE inflation, economists say
sources.evidence_text: Reuters reports that some economists expect methodological changes could revise May core PCE slightly lower, including Goldman Sachs and JPMorgan estimates around 3.2% to 3.3%.
sources.why_it_matters: If the official core PCE trend is revised down, that would reduce pressure on the Fed to keep policy tight.

sources.title: The Fed - Inflation (PCE) - Federal Reserve Board
sources.evidence_text: The Fed states that it seeks 2% inflation over the longer run as measured by PCE.
sources.why_it_matters: This defines the benchmark the Fed uses to judge whether inflation is still too high for an easing bias.

sources.title: Markets expected the rate cut, but the ‘real surprise' is the Fed's opinion on the current state of the economy, quant CEO says
sources.evidence_text: The story says markets expected the Fed’s 25-basis-point cut and then focused on the Fed’s updated view of the economy rather than the cut itself.
sources.why_it_matters: When cuts are already priced, the policy signal matters more than the move, because the reaction function turns on whether the Fed sees more or fewer cuts ahead.

sources.title: June 16-17, 2026 FOMC Meeting Statement
sources.evidence_text: The FOMC left the federal funds target range unchanged at 3.5% to 3.75% and said it would continue to assess incoming data and the balance of risks.
sources.why_it_matters: A hold signals no immediate shift toward easier policy, so the statement is neutral for the near-term cut-vs-hike debate.

sources.title: Fed's Goolsbee says labor market stable, inflation going wrong way
sources.evidence_text: Reuters reported that Goolsbee described the labor market as steady but said inflation is moving in the wrong direction and that the key question is whether the spike will prove temporary.
sources.why_it_matters: If a policymaker views inflation as sticky while labor conditions remain stable, the reaction function leans away from cuts and toward patience or restraint.

sources.title: Fed Preview: Next Man Up
sources.evidence_text: Investing.com says the Fed is likely to hold rates steady, but the main risk is that officials remove any easing bias from the statement.
sources.why_it_matters: Removing easing bias would suggest the Fed is less inclined to cut soon and more willing to keep policy restrictive.

sources.title: US jobless claims fall to 187,000, lowest since 1969, supporting rate-hike bets
sources.evidence_text: Initial claims fell to 187,000, the lowest level in decades, indicating very little layoffs-driven cooling in the labor market.
sources.why_it_matters: Very low claims imply labor-market resilience, which reduces the Fed's justification for cuts and increases the perceived risk of tighter policy.

sources.title: Jobless Claims Fall to 57-Year Low, Pushing Fed Rate-Hike Odds Past One-in-Three
sources.evidence_text: The article said the claims print strengthened the case for at least one additional Fed hike later in 2026.
sources.why_it_matters: Market and media interpretation that claims are too low for comfort suggests less easing pressure and a higher bar for rate cuts.

sources.title: Revamp of 'core' PCE measure could help Fed estimate underlying inflation
sources.evidence_text: St. Louis Fed research argued that including food and utility prices in core PCE could better capture underlying inflation.
sources.why_it_matters: If policymakers put more weight on broader underlying price pressures, it would reduce tolerance for easing while inflation stays sticky.

sources.title: Inflation Expectations
sources.evidence_text: The Cleveland Fed publishes model-based estimates of expected inflation, inflation risk premia, and the real interest rate using Treasury yields, inflation data, inflation swaps, and survey measures.
sources.why_it_matters: Market-based and model-based inflation expectations help the Fed judge whether inflation credibility is improving or whether policy needs to remain restrictive.

sources.title: CPI Inflation Contributions from Goods and Services
sources.publisher: Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco
sources.evidence_text: The San Francisco Fed tracks how goods and services contribute to CPI inflation, providing a way to monitor whether services inflation remains the main source of price pressure.
sources.why_it_matters: Persistent services-led inflation would argue for a more restrictive Fed stance because it is harder to unwind than transitory goods price moves.

sources.title: Inflation surprise pushes rate cut odds down
sources.evidence_text: Core PCE rose 0.3% on the month and 2.8% year over year, above expectations, and the article says markets reduced the odds of a September cut.
sources.why_it_matters: A hotter-than-expected Fed-preferred inflation gauge directly argues for fewer or later cuts in the reaction function.

sources.title: Why a CPI surprise could trip up the Fed's rate-cutting plans
sources.evidence_text: The article says an upside CPI surprise could push the Fed toward a pause in rate cuts and keep the policy rate unchanged at the next meeting.
sources.why_it_matters: If inflation surprises higher, the Fed is more likely to delay easing to preserve credibility on price stability.

sources.title: Inflation edges up, highlighting Fed's bumpy path to stable prices
sources.evidence_text: The article says October CPI rose to 2.6% year over year, which it described as a bump that still likely would not change the Fed's near-term course.
sources.why_it_matters: A firmer inflation print reduces the Fed's room to cut aggressively even if it does not fully reverse the easing cycle.

sources.title: Speech by Vice Chair Jefferson on navigating economic conditions
sources.evidence_text: Jefferson said the FOMC kept the federal funds target range at 3-1/2 to 3-3/4 percent in June and that this stance should support the labor market while inflation continues moving back toward 2 percent.
sources.why_it_matters: This signals a wait-and-see reaction function: the Fed is not adding restraint, but it is also not yet signaling faster easing.

sources.title: Monetary Policy and the Fed's Framework Review
sources.evidence_text: Powell said policy was already much closer to neutral than a year earlier and that labor-market stability allowed the Fed to proceed carefully with further changes.
sources.why_it_matters: A closer-to-neutral stance and stable employment tend to keep the door open to additional easing if inflation cooperates.

sources.title: Treasury yields jump as traders take out expectations for any 2026 Fed rate cuts
sources.evidence_text: The article says traders in fed-funds futures cut the probability of any Fed rate reduction this year to 8.8% and started pricing in the possibility of hikes by April.
sources.why_it_matters: Pricing out cuts and adding hike probability shifts market conditions toward restraint, signaling that the expected policy path is no longer easing.

sources.title: Fed Rate Monitor
sources.evidence_text: Fisclear’s Fed monitor shows a 70% implied probability that the July 28–29 meeting ends with no change and a 30% probability of a 25 bp hike.
sources.why_it_matters: A hold-dominant OIS setup implies markets still expect the Fed to avoid immediate tightening, though a nontrivial hike tail remains.

sources.title: OIS Contracts Indicate 25 Basis Point Rate Cut by September FOMC Meeting
sources.evidence_text: The article says OIS contracts are fully pricing a 25 basis point cut by the September FOMC meeting and about 62 basis points of cuts across the remaining three meetings this year.
sources.why_it_matters: If the market is fully priced for cuts, that signals easing expectations in the policy path and pressures the Fed reaction function toward validating weaker-growth, softer-labor-market outcomes.

sources.title: U.S. weekly jobless claims rise to 243,000, highest in eight weeks
sources.evidence_text: Initial jobless claims rose to 243,000 for the week ending July 13, and continuing claims increased to about 1.87 million.
sources.why_it_matters: Higher claims and more people staying on benefits suggest some labor-market cooling, which can reduce wage pressure and support Fed cuts.

sources.title: Trimmed Mean PCE inflation rate
sources.evidence_text: The Dallas Fed's trimmed mean PCE measure was 2.4% over the 12 months ending in May.
sources.why_it_matters: A near-target trimmed mean reading suggests underlying inflation is closer to acceptable levels than headline PCE, tempering the case for additional tightening.

sources.title: Survey of Consumer Expectations, June 2026
sources.publisher: Federal Reserve Bank of New York
sources.evidence_text: The New York Fed’s June survey showed near-term and longer-term inflation expectations little changed from prior months.
sources.why_it_matters: Stable expectations reduce the risk of a wage-price spiral, but they do not by themselves justify faster easing.

sources.title: July 2026 Monetary Policy Report discussion of expectations and futures pricing
sources.evidence_text: The Fed reported that federal funds futures implied rates around 4% by year-end 2026, above the current effective rate.
sources.why_it_matters: Market pricing for a higher policy path signals less confidence in rapid easing and can reinforce cautious Fed behavior.

sources.title: Transcript of Chair Powell's Press Conference -- June 17, 2026
sources.evidence_text: Powell said inflation remained elevated, the labor market had stabilized after softening, and the Committee kept the policy rate unchanged after earlier cuts.
sources.why_it_matters: This signaled a pause rather than an immediate easing bias, because the Fed was still prioritizing inflation progress while acknowledging firmer labor conditions.

sources.title: U.S. Treasury yields rise as traders bet on Fed rate hikes
sources.evidence_text: The article says the 2-year Treasury yield rose to a 16-month high as traders bet the Fed may need to raise rates later this year, with futures assigning a meaningful hike probability.
sources.why_it_matters: A new high in the 2-year yield alongside hike bets indicates the market is repricing toward tighter Fed policy and fewer expected cuts.
